question: What type of data is primarily gathered during a patient health history interview?

options.A: Surgical findings from the operating room

explanation: Health history relies on what the patient says and feels, which is classified as subjective data. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is gathering a thorough health history considered the foundation of patient care?

options.A: It guides clinical reasoning and nursing interventions
options.B: It guarantees the patient will recover quickly
options.C: It completely replaces the need for physical exams
options.D: It provides all necessary laboratory values

explanation: A complete history helps nurses understand the patient's condition so they can plan safe, effective care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which question type is best for encouraging a patient to tell their story in their own words?
explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to elaborate freely without limiting their responses to a single word. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient looks down and hesitates when asked about alcohol use. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Maintain a calm, non-judgmental attitude and wait patiently
options.B: Scold the patient for hiding information
options.C: Move on immediately to a different topic to avoid embarrassment
options.D: Document that the patient is being uncooperative

explanation: Showing patience and a non-judgmental stance helps build trust so the patient feels safe sharing sensitive details. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the chief complaint in a patient health history?

options.B: The results of the patient's blood work
options.C: The main reason the patient is seeking care
options.D: A list of all medications taken in the past year

explanation: The chief complaint captures the primary problem or symptom that brought the patient to the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is recording past medical and surgical history important during an admission assessment?

options.A: It replaces the need to ask about current medications
options.B: It predicts the exact date the patient will be discharged
options.C: It proves the patient has visited a hospital before
options.D: It helps identify chronic conditions that may affect current treatment

explanation: Knowing past health problems helps the healthcare team anticipate complications and tailor current therapy safely. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does the letter 'L' stand for in the OLDCARTS mnemonic used for symptom analysis?
explanation: Location refers to the exact anatomical site where the patient feels the symptom. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient reports sharp chest pain that gets worse when taking a deep breath. Which part of OLDCARTS does 'worse when taking a deep breath' represent?
explanation: Anything that triggers or increases the intensity of a symptom is classified as an aggravating factor. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h4)

question: When taking a family history, which relatives are most important to include?

options.D: Immediate family members like parents, siblings, and children

explanation: Immediate family members share the closest genetic link, making their health history most relevant for hereditary risks. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important to ask about past surgical complications, such as a bad reaction to anesthesia?

options.A: To calculate the exact hospital bill in advance
options.B: To check if the patient has valid health insurance
options.C: To prevent similar dangerous reactions during future procedures
options.D: To determine what food the patient likes to eat

explanation: Knowing about previous adverse anesthesia reactions allows the surgical and anesthesia team to take safety precautions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of the review of systems in health history taking?

options.A: To perform the physical hands-on examination of the body
options.B: To discharge the patient from the hospital ward
options.C: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or overlooked
options.D: To administer prescribed medications to the patient

explanation: The review of systems uses a systematic checklist to catch extra details the patient did not bring up initially. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following findings belongs in the review of systems?

options.A: A patient reporting occasional dizziness when standing up
options.B: A nurse measuring a blood pressure reading of 120/80 mmHg
options.C: A laboratory report showing a high white blood cell count
options.D: A surgeon finding an inflamed appendix during an operation

explanation: Dizziness reported by the patient is a subjective symptom, which is what the review of systems records. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which topic is typically evaluated during a psychosocial and lifestyle assessment?

options.A: Tobacco, alcohol, and substance use habits
options.C: Detailed cellular structure of body tissues
options.D: Exact surgical technique used in an operation

explanation: Lifestyle assessments cover daily habits, including substance use, diet, exercise, and stress levels. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why must nurses ask patients about their home environment and social support before discharge?

options.A: To find out if the patient's house has modern furniture
options.B: To decide whether the patient should pay cash or use credit
options.C: To ensure the patient has the help needed to manage recovery safely
options.D: To report neighborhood safety issues to the local police

explanation: Understanding home support and living conditions helps nurses plan realistic and safe post-discharge care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which statement represents objective, professional documentation in a health record?

options.A: Patient states left knee pain is 8 out of 10
options.B: Patient is just complaining to get extra attention
options.C: Patient is having a terrible day in the ward
options.D: Patient looks lazy and refuses to walk today

explanation: Recording what the patient specifically stated avoids personal bias and maintains professional documentation standards. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the main legal reason why patient health records must be accurate and timely?

options.A: Patients use them as textbooks for nursing school exams
options.B: Hospital managers check them daily to give out staff bonuses
options.C: Medical records are legal documents used in healthcare and legal proceedings
options.D: Insurance companies use them to advertise hospital services

explanation: Because health records are legal documents, accurate and prompt documentation protects both the patient and the healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h8)
